LanguageData.RMush_PoisonFlyAgaric.stages.0.label: asymptomatic
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonFlyAgaric.stages.1.label: confused and drowsy
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonFlyAgaric.stages.2.label: impaired consciousness
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonFlyAgaric.stages.3.label: severe neurological poisoning
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonFlyAgaric.stages.4.label: profound drowsiness
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonFlyAgaric.label: fly agaric poisoning
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonFlyAgaric.description: Confusion, drowsiness and impaired consciousness; severe poisoning can leave the victim unable to act. Symptoms resolve gradually after onset. Ordinary medical care can speed recovery.
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonDestroyingAngel.label: destroying angel poisoning
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonDestroyingAngel.description: Delayed gastrointestinal symptoms followed by progressive liver injury. Symptoms appearing to ease do not mean the poisoning has stopped. Untreated poisoning can be fatal. Care must be repeated using the normal medical system. Recovery is gradual after stabilization. After the first symptom warning, a single exposure grants at least 24 hours before this poisoning itself can enter its lethal stage. Other illnesses, injuries and additional exposures are not covered.
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonSulfurTuft.stages.0.label: asymptomatic
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonSulfurTuft.stages.1.label: stomach pain
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonSulfurTuft.stages.2.label: gastroenteritis and weakness
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonSulfurTuft.stages.3.label: severe gastroenteritis
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonSulfurTuft.stages.4.label: profound weakness
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonSulfurTuft.label: sulfur tuft poisoning
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonSulfurTuft.description: Persistent severe gastroenteritis, vomiting, pain and weakness. More severe poisoning needs medical care and takes longer to recover. Symptoms resolve gradually after onset. Ordinary medical care can speed recovery.
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonTsukiyotake.stages.0.label: asymptomatic
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonTsukiyotake.stages.1.label: acute nausea
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonTsukiyotake.stages.2.label: vomiting and enteritis
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonTsukiyotake.stages.3.label: severe enteritis
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonTsukiyotake.stages.4.label: severe enteritis and weakness
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonTsukiyotake.label: tsukiyotake poisoning
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonTsukiyotake.description: Rapid, strong vomiting followed by lingering enteritis and weakness. Severe intestinal symptoms, including intestinal bleeding symptoms, are represented in-game as pain and weakness rather than separate blood loss. Symptoms resolve gradually after onset. Ordinary medical care can speed recovery.
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonPoisonFireCoral.label: poison fire coral poisoning
LanguageData.RMush_PoisonPoisonFireCoral.description: Progressive systemic poisoning with vomiting, pain, weakness, reduced immunity gain and impaired consciousness. Untreated or late-treated poisoning can be fatal. Care must be repeated using the normal medical system. Recovery is gradual after stabilization. After the first symptom warning, a single exposure grants at least 24 hours before this poisoning itself can enter its lethal stage. Other illnesses, injuries and additional exposures are not covered.
